name: Token bucket
brief: `rate` tokens a second refill continuously, up to `burst` tokens. The bucket starts full. `allow(now_ns)` is called with non-decreasing times in nanoseconds. It returns true and spends one token if a whole token is available, else false. Use integers only: no floating point.
constraints: Times are `long long` nanoseconds and never go backwards.
Do not use floating point: ten refills of 0.1 of a token do not add up to exactly 1.
hint: Count tokens in billionths: each elapsed nanosecond adds `rate` units, and one token is 1,000,000,000 units. Cap the total at `burst` tokens.

examples.name: A burst of three
examples.note: The bucket starts full with 3 tokens, so a fourth call at the same instant is refused.

examples.name: Refill
examples.note: At 1,000 tokens a second, one token returns every 1,000,000 ns.

tests.name: A burst of three
tests.note: The bucket starts full with 3 tokens, so a fourth call at the same instant is refused.

tests.name: Refill
tests.note: At 1,000 tokens a second, one token returns every 1,000,000 ns.

how: Ten hidden tests call `allow` with lists of times: bursts, refills, refused calls and a refill every 0.1 s. Others use a rate of one token a nanosecond, times of 10^12 ns and a gap of 20 s. A hidden driver returns 1 for an allowed call and 0 for a refused one.
notes: Update the clock on every call, even a refused one.
Counting in billionths of a token keeps the arithmetic exact.
